mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate over the past month signals an accommodative monetary policy stance, reducing the cost of capital and boosting equity valuations, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of instances when FEDFUNDS is declining, or the Rank IC over 3 years is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate rises above 6.5% in a 3-month window, it signals deteriorating labor market conditions that reduce consumer spending and corporate earnings, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 40% of instances when UNRATE exceeds 6.5%, or the Rank IC is negative over any 2-year window.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in housing starts and consumer spending (measured by RSAFS) indicate a weakening demand environment that triggers a sell-off in equities, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of instances when both HOUST and RSAFS decline, or the interaction term's coefficient is not significant (p>0.05) in a regression.

mechanism_narrative: During periods of high inflation (CPIAUCSL > 2.5% year-over-year), the Federal Reserve is likely to tighten monetary policy, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 50% of instances when CPIAUCSL y/y > 2.5%, or the Rank IC over 3 years is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in industrial production (INDPRO) above 102.5 for two consecutive months indicates robust economic activity, which supports corporate earnings growth and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in more than 60% of instances when INDPRO is above 102.5, or the Rank IC is below 0.03 over any 1-year window.

mechanism_narrative: When housing starts (HOUST) fall below 900 thousand units for two consecutive months, it signals a contraction in the housing market that reduces consumer wealth and spending, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST falls < 900 thousand units for 2 months
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 40% of instances when HOUST < 900, or the Rank IC is negative over 2 years.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous increases in unemployment rate (UNRATE) and declines in non-farm payrolls (PAYEMS) indicate a weakening labor market that reduces consumer confidence and spending, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of instances when UNRATE rises and PAYEMS falls, or the interaction term's coefficient is not significant (p>0.05).

mechanism_narrative: During periods of strong consumer spending (RSAFS growth > 1.0% monthly), the S&P 500 tends to rise over the next 60 trading days as corporate revenues and profits expand.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are negative in more than 50% of instances when RSAFS growth > 1.0%, or the Rank IC over 3 years is below 0.03.
